en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘For Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic there are two (types of) Knowledges. There is a Knowledge with Him<sup>azwj</sup> which He<sup>azwj</sup> has not Notified upon anyone from His<sup>azwj</sup> creatures with it. And there is a Knowledge which He<sup>saww</sup> Cast to His<sup>azwj</sup> Angels, and His<sup>azwj</sup> Rasools<sup>as</sup>. So whatever He<sup>azwj</sup> Cast to His<sup>azwj</sup> Angels and His<sup>azwj</sup> Rasools<sup>as</sup>, so it has ended up to us<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn abu Hamzah from abu Basir from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.

“Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, has two kinds of knowledge. One kind is His only and no creature knows about it. The other kind is that which He has thrown unto His angels and His Messenger. Whatever is thrown to the angels and the Messengers have reached us.”
